title: Universal device action bridge
request: Turn the Termux plus Chrome connection into a permanent, network-independent, reusable IMA device capability and product.
work_completed_today: Inspected the current Termux Chrome bridge, public live-browser UI, plugin registry, device architecture, rights and revenue governance.
Confirmed the existing public IMA chat already contains a live browser workspace that can display the real Chrome screen when the local bridge is available.
Added an owner-scoped device command plane backed by the active IMA Supabase project.
Added one-time device-key issuance with server-side hashing and revocation.
Added transactional command claiming, expiring commands and result reporting.
Added a reusable outbound-only Termux device agent that works across changing Wi-Fi and cellular networks.
Connected the device agent to the existing Chrome CDP bridge and Android AccessibilityService command contract.
Added the Universal Device Bridge safety policy and capability registry entry.
Added the IMA-specific Universal Action Bridge architecture and breakthrough record.
Created the first private IMA Universal Device Bridge plugin distribution artifact.
Extended IMA rights/provenance records to cover the new capability.
research_findings: The general concept is not unique: browser agents, WebMCP, Android accessibility bridges and outbound device relays already exist.

The differentiating IMA formulation is the unified provider-neutral action layer combined with evidence-gated capability promotion, consent, revocation, continuity, adaptive interface selection and post-action verification.
WebMCP is an emerging browser standard for structured agent tools and should be added to IMA's preferred execution ladder.
Android background execution remains a real production constraint; Termux:Boot, foreground execution and device-specific battery settings must be verified rather than promised.
remaining_gates: Run live registration and end-to-end command tests on Ori's current phone.
Add a user-facing device management and consent UI.
Harden Android always-on lifecycle and reconnect behavior.
Add independent security testing and abuse-case tests.
Complete MCP/provider review before claiming public publication.
Validate pricing and real customer demand before declaring commercial success.
next_learning_rule: Every future IMA improvement cycle must inspect historical requirements, current runtime evidence and new external developments, then prefer verified, reversible improvements without duplicating existing capabilities.
